note: Cases mirror the archived closed_circuit.rs viewer_stranded_* tests (validate_viewer_stranded_for_owner, body_offers_way_on, trait_offers_way_on, RenderScope same-arm resolution) with paired controls. Each case replays the six inputs the rule waits for (pattern kinds, event props, bus-excluded events, the program, the page owners from std-orb-lint-page-content-owner, the fired events from std-orb-fired-events) and the compute. Expected findings are the code, path, message and suggestion the Rust validator reports for the same program.

findings.message: 'Owner' owns this page's content region, and 'STRAND' repaints it with a body that carries no data surface, no wired control and no sibling embed — the screen the viewer came from is gone and there is nothing to click
findings.suggestion: render this OVER the page instead of replacing it: move the body into a dedicated overlay trait writing only 'modal' (a modal-close arm rendered from the trait that owns 'main' is rejected by CIRCUIT_MODAL_EXIT_INCOMPLETE, which is why it needs its own trait), or give the arm a wired control back to the state it came from
